The Spinning Jenny

8

A In 1733, John Kay invented the Flying Shuttle. This invention more than doubled the speed and efficiency of weaving.

The construction of a spinning machine

B Hargreaves built the Spinning Jenny on a simple frame made of wood. Eight spindles were fixed at one end. The operator turned a handwheel, which pulled a cord to drive a roller. A moving carriage pulled threads from the rovings back and forth.

C Simple machines can transform everyday work. The Jenny could spin eight threads in the time that a conventional spinning wheel produced one.
